mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% over a two-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% in any two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (core inflation) over two months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month MA for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE over a three-month period indicates robust labor market expansion with low unemployment, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE falls below 5% simultaneously over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls below 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An above-consensus increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS rising >5% YoY for two consecutive months) amid stable GDP growth (GDPC1 flat) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a future consumption-led rebound and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +5% YoY for two months and GDPC1 flat
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises >5% YoY for two months and GDPC1 is flat.
